question: A 17-year-old girl suddenly grabs her chest and collapses to the ground while playing volleyball at school. The teacher rushes to evaluate the situation and finds that the girl has no pulse and is not breathing. He starts chest compressions. An automated external defibrillator (AED) is brought to the scene within 3 minutes and a shock is delivered. The girl regains consciousness and regular sinus rhythm. She is rushed to the emergency department. The vital signs include: blood pressure 122/77 mm Hg and pulse 65/min. The pulse is regular. An electrocardiogram (ECG) shows a shortened PR interval, a wide QRS complex, a delta wave, and an inverted T wave. Which of the following is the most likely pathology in the conduction system of this patient’s heart?

options.opa: Automatic discharge of irregular impulses in the atria
options.opb: Impulse generation by tissue in atrioventricular node
options.opd: Accessory pathway from atria to ventricles

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Shortened PR interval, wide QRS complex, delta wave, inverted T wave on ECG" -> "Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome" -> "Accessory pathway from atria to ventricles" -> 95% CHAIN: "Chest pain, collapse, no pulse, not breathing" -> "Sudden cardiac arrest" -> "Accessory pathway from atria to ventricles" -> 90% CHAIN: "AED shock delivered, regains consciousness, regular sinus rhythm" -> "Successful termination of arrhythmia" -> "Accessory pathway from atria to ventricles" -> 95%
analysis: The ECG findings of a shortened PR interval, wide QRS complex, delta wave, and inverted T wave are characteristic of Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome. WPW syndrome is caused by an accessory pathway (Bundle of Kent) that allows for abnormal conduction between the atria and ventricles, leading to the characteristic ECG findings and potential risk of reentrant tachyarrhythmias.
